title: Hyper slowness issue
body: I built curl with -DUSE_HYPER on Windows 10. Fetching three ADSB route URLs takes at least a minute, with long pauses between responses, whether the URLs are supplied on the command line or through a config file and whether or not I use --parallel. The curl bundled with Windows completes the same transfers in under a second. Updating Rust and rebuilding current Hyper did not help.

symptoms_visible: A curl build using Hyper takes at least one minute to fetch three route URLs, with long pauses between them; the Windows-bundled curl completes the same work in under one second, and --parallel does not remove the pauses.
N0.label: N0 Hyper transfer slowness reported

symptoms_visible: The same Hyper-specific delay is reproducible on Linux; tracing shows a response becomes available immediately when the Hyper executor is polled a second time instead of waiting for a later transfer-loop call.
N1.label: N1 cross-platform reproduction and executor observation

symptoms_visible: After rebuilding with the changes from PR 11344, the reporter still sees roughly minute-long transfers and long pauses between responses.
N2_x.label: N2_x PR 11344 aftermath

symptoms_visible: The first response arrives immediately, followed by approximately 30-second pauses before later responses; in some runs a response is absent.
For the same endpoints, forcing HTTP/1.1 completes in about 300 ms while the Hyper HTTP/2 path takes over a minute.
The trace does not show a new connection being opened during the pauses.
N3.label: N3 delay isolated to Hyper HTTP2 path

symptoms_visible: A packet capture shows the Hyper build sending an HTTP/2 connection preface and settings before each of the three requests on the same connection, unlike the normal backend, which sends one preface followed by all three requests.
N4.label: N4 repeated HTTP2 prefaces identify lifecycle defect

symptoms_visible: After rebuilding current Hyper and curl master with Hyper HTTP/2 disabled, the three transfers complete in about one second instead of over a minute; a later run is only about 20 percent slower than the Windows-bundled curl.
N5.label: N5 temporary fix verified on master

symptoms_visible: Curl master uses HTTP/1.1 for the Hyper backend, and the reporter's three-URL test now completes in about one second without the previous 30-second gaps or missing response.
N_terminal.label: terminal Hyper slowness mitigated

question_patterns: Can this be reproduced outside Windows?
Does a Hyper-enabled Linux build show the same delays?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. Other affected testers reproduce it on Linux: normal curl finishes in one or two seconds, while curl with Hyper takes about a minute.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: No; it only happens on this Windows machine, and the same Hyper build is fast on Linux.

question_patterns: What does tracing Curl_hyper_stream and hyper_executor_poll show during the pause?
What happens if the Hyper executor is polled again immediately after HYPER_TASK_EMPTY?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: After socket input is processed, the first hyper_executor_poll returns HYPER_TASK_EMPTY. Calling it a second time immediately returns HYPER_TASK_RESPONSE and makes the transfers fast; otherwise curl waits for a later transfer-loop call.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The second poll returns the response after a few milliseconds rather than immediately.

edges.comment: Thread c1-c2: Linux reproduction and executor instrumentation came from other participants. All affected testers are folded into one simulated user side.

solution.intent: Apply the initial Hyper integration changes from PR 11344, based on the executor and waker observations, as the fix for the long pauses.
solution.concrete_example: Rebuild curl with PR 11344, which adjusts the Hyper integration based on upstream advice and the observed executor behavior, then rerun the three-URL test.

edges.comment: Thread c7-c8: PR 11344 resolved the developer's local case but did not fix the reporter's reproduction, so it cannot be accepted as the case resolution.

question_patterns: Can you provide timestamped output showing where the minute is spent?
Do all three responses arrive slowly, or are there regular gaps between them?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The first response arrives immediately. Then there is a pause of about 30 seconds before the second response and another approximately 30-second pause before the third.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The pauses are about 25 seconds rather than exactly 30, but still occur between the second and third requests.

question_patterns: Do all requested responses eventually appear?
Is this only slow, or is any response missing?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: In some runs one of the three responses is missing as well as the run taking about a minute.

question_patterns: Can you compare the Hyper HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 paths on the same endpoints?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. With Hyper, the default HTTP/2 path takes over 60 seconds for these endpoints, while adding --http1.1 completes in roughly 300 ms. Other HTTP/2 endpoints vary, with some completing in a few seconds.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Forcing --http1.1 still takes over a minute with the same 30-second gaps.
The JSON fields are returned in a different order under HTTP/1.1.

question_patterns: Does the timestamped trace show curl opening a new connection after the pause?
Could the 30-second delay be a TLS timeout followed by a silent reconnect?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: No. The trace shows no new connection, and curl does not report a failed transfer followed by a reconnect.

edges.comment: Thread c9-c17 and c23: timestamped traces and protocol-forcing measurements isolate the severe behavior to the Hyper HTTP/2 path. Reports from multiple affected users are merged.

question_patterns: Can you inspect the HTTP/2 traffic with Wireshark and SSLKEYLOGFILE?
How does the sequence of HTTP/2 frames differ between the normal backend and Hyper?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The normal backend sends one HTTP/2 connection preface, settings/window update, and then requests 1, 2, and 3. The Hyper backend sends a connection preface and settings again before each request on the same connection.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The packet capture shows exactly one connection preface followed normally by all three requests for both backends.
The repeated settings frames have slightly different window sizes, but Hyper still sends a new connection preface before every request.

edges.comment: Thread c23-c41: the packet capture grounds the diagnosis. Engineers infer that curl creates a hyper_clientconn per request, producing invalid repeated HTTP/2 prefaces; server GOAWAY handling then delays, retries, or drops requests. Because correctly persisting the Hyper connection object conflicts with curl transfer and multiplexing lifecycles, disabling Hyper HTTP/2 is proposed as the safe temporary fix.

question_patterns: Can you rebuild current curl master after the Hyper HTTP/2 disablement and rerun the three-URL benchmark?
Does the build containing PR 12191 remove the minute-long pauses and missing response?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. After updating Hyper and curl master, the same three transfers take about 1.137 seconds instead of over a minute. A later rebuild takes 0.974 seconds versus 0.803 seconds for the Windows-bundled curl, with no 30-second gaps reported.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The master build with Hyper HTTP/2 disabled still takes over a minute and still loses a response.
The fixed build takes 1.3 seconds rather than 1.1 seconds, but the long gaps and missing response are gone.

edges.comment: Thread c42 and c44-c46: PR 12191 disabled HTTP/2 for Hyper, and the reporter verified current master. This is a handler-provided build measurement, so it remains a clarification-only edge.

solution.intent: Ship the safe temporary mitigation from PR 12191: disable HTTP/2 in the Hyper backend so requests use reusable HTTP/1.1 connections, while documenting that restoring Hyper HTTP/2 requires a connection-lifecycle rearchitecture.
solution.concrete_example: Keep HTTP/2 disabled for USE_HYPER and use HTTP/1.1, which the reporter verified removes the minute-long gaps. Do not recreate a hyper_clientconn for each HTTP/2 request. Restoring HTTP/2 requires keeping the Hyper client connection for the actual connection lifetime, likely by redesigning the integration around curl connection filters and multiplexed-transfer lookup.

edges.comment: Resolved behavior is the severe slowness and dropped-response issue. HTTP/2 remains disabled for the Hyper backend as a documented limitation; a full Hyper HTTP/2 restoration requires larger architectural work.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the true root cause: curl's Hyper integration created a hyper_clientconn for each request on a reused HTTP/2 connection, causing a new HTTP/2 connection preface and settings to be sent before every request; this invalid sequence can provoke server GOAWAY behavior, delayed retries, or dropped requests.

Must ground the diagnosis in the collected evidence: HTTP/1.1 is fast while the Hyper HTTP/2 path has approximately 30-second gaps, no replacement connection appears in the trace, and the packet capture shows repeated HTTP/2 prefaces.
Must not present updating Rust or Hyper, polling the executor twice, or PR 11344 as the resolution; fresh rebuilds and PR 11344 did not resolve the reporter's case.

The accepted mitigation must disable HTTP/2 for the Hyper backend and fall back to HTTP/1.1, while acknowledging that restoring Hyper HTTP/2 requires correct connection-lifetime persistence or a connection-filter rearchitecture.
Must require reporter verification of the patched master build, showing the transfer reduced from over a minute to about one second without the long gaps, before declaring the slowness resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Highly technical curl contributor and Windows C developer who builds curl, Hyper, and multiple TLS backends from source; comfortable supplying scripts, traces, timings, debug assertions, and rebuild results, but defers on Hyper and curl state-machine internals.
persona_hint.communication_style: Direct, concise, and evidence-driven. Provides reproducible commands and timing comparisons, follows up after rebuilding, and plainly says when a proposed fix does not work.
